messages.author: 394838c3712aced6
messages.subject: Poisson IRT model
parts: I'm interested in estimating a Zero-inflated Poisson-IRT model (https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.3102/1076998610375838) to estimate the structure of a set of count variables. I was wondering whether it might be possible to implement this item type. It's not immediately clear to me whether the Poisson part of the model (Equations 1a and 1b in the linked paper) can be implemented using the `createItem()` function.

messages.author: 58786c912f9ee9c2
messages.subject: Re: Poisson IRT model
parts:
Hi Brenton,

I do not know whether mirt can do it. However, we have used the R-package glmmTMB for similar purposes. You have to see the model as a generalized linear mixed model, with the person parameter being the only random effect.

-Philipp

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Poisson IRT model
parts:
I don't see why this couldn't work with the createItem() function. You should just need to write out the probability form in the author's equation 3 as the positive endorsement value (the second column) and 1 minus this second column to obtain the P(y=0) expectations. There's likely some numerical tricks to watch out for in these specifications, but inherently I do not see any major issues.

Phil
